text:
alex_support: FYI customer on Private deployment (VPC, us-east-1) reports streaming responses drop after ~30-40s of silence. They're using a third-party edge appliance (F5) in front of their app. Client sees net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET, server logs show 'websocket: close 1006 (abnormal closure): EOF'.
sara_cs: Do we have any patterns on Private endpoints + middleboxes? Sounds like idle timeout / proxy buffering.
josh_infra: Can you get a minimal repro? Ask them to run wscat to our endpoint and reproduce. Also need tcpdump from the edge and our side. Typical culprit: proxy configured to terminate TLS or buffer and close idle connections ~30s.
alex_support: Customer sent quick repro steps: "wscat -c wss://private-123.redwood-infra.example.com/stream" -> stream starts, then stop sending traffic for 35s, connection drops. They also tried curl --no-buffer -N and saw gap then reset.
li_engineering: Two quick checks: 1) Does the F5/edge do TLS termination (i.e. breaks end-to-end TLS)? 2) Is there an explicit connection idle timeout (30s is common)? If TLS is terminated at the proxy, the proxy may be closing the backend connection to our routing tier.
sara_cs: Customer confirms TLS is rewrapped at F5 (TLS offload then re-encrypt to backend). They also have an App Gateway that applies HTTP/2 <-> HTTP/1.1 translation for backend.
josh_infra: Actionable asks for customer: capture a short tcpdump on the edge during repro: sudo tcpdump -i any host private-123.redwood-infra.example.com and include timestamps. Also capture backend side (our Private connector VM) if they can. Look for FIN/RST from the appliance.
alex_support: Customer provided small excerpt of tcpdump: "14:22:10.123456 IP edge -> app 443: Flags [P.], seq 1:520, ack 1, win 64240
14:22:45.456789 IP app -> edge 443: Flags [R], seq 1, ack 1, win 0" — shows RST from their appliance at ~35s.
li_engineering: That looks like active close at the appliance. Workarounds: - Configure the appliance idle timeout to something higher (e.g., 10m) OR enable passthrough TLS so no backend connection is closed on idle. - If passthrough not possible, enable keepalive pings on the client (application-level ping) or TCP keepalives: setsockopt SO_KEEPALIVE + TCP_KEEPIDLE 20.
josh_infra: Also ask them to disable proxy buffering / response buffering and ensure proxy honors chunked transfer without buffering. For nginx-like proxies: proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 600; proxy_send_timeout 600. For F5, set 'OneConnect' / idle timeout config.
sara_cs: I suggested a quick test: run wscat and send a tiny ping every 20s (or client library keepalive) and confirm connection stays alive past 2m.
alex_support: Customer ran ping strategy and connection stayed open. They changed F5 idle timeout from 30s to 300s and confirmed stable. They want permanent fix guidance.
li_engineering: Final recommendations to paste to customer: 1) Prefer TLS passthrough to preserve end-to-end websockets if possible. 2) If TLS offload required, increase idle timeouts on edge to >= 300s and disable response buffering for streaming routes. 3) Use application-level pings (WS ping/pong) and/or enable TCP keepalives. 4) On our Private side, ensure we advertise no aggressive idle close and document recommended timeout knobs for common appliances (F5, HAProxy, nginx, Azure Application Gateway).
josh_infra: I'll add a short KB note in support docs with commands: tcpdump snippet, openssl s_client check (openssl s_client -connect private-123.redwood-infra.example.com:443 -servername private-123.redwood-infra.example.com -quiet) and sample nginx/F5 settings.
deploy-bot: deploy status: doc-kb/edge-timeouts added to support bucket (PR #482). :white_check_mark:
sara_cs: Closing loop with customer, asked them to file a change request with their network team to keep idle timeout >= 300s. Customer happy. :thumbsup:
